sourceStates.title: [levanter] Preserve final checkpoints across forced saves
sourceStates.body:
Keep the latest checkpoint loadable when the final forced hook follows a temporary save or a completed-run restart. Promote an existing temporary checkpoint by changing only its metadata after the pending save completes. Replace local manifests atomically so an interrupted restart leaves the prior manifest intact; object-store writes remain direct because a rename requires a copy and delete.

A CPU crash injection on `main` at `cb991a5` left the default temporary step and the restarted step unloadable. With this change, the default step is promoted without a re-save, and the restarted step still loads after a crash while its replacement manifest is open. Multi-process runs and a crash during array rewriting on restart remain untested.

Fixes #11959
Fixes #11534

sourceStates.title: [skyrl] Preserve NCCL AllGather in learner processes
sourceStates.body:
Permit Ring for NCCL collectives outside all-reduce while retaining Tree for batch-invariant all-reduce in SkyRL's learner processes. The [November 21 SkyRL nightly](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44925403052/job/136910257408) failed in Grug's two-rank eval test during Megatron optimizer initialization: `all_gather_object` had no available algorithm because `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` named only the all-reduce function.

The [pinned vLLM initializer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py#L1142-L1155) overwrites the Ray learner's `NCCL_ALGO` during actor construction. SkyRL now reapplies the Ring fallback after that call, before Megatron creates its process groups. The [targeted H100 rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930085809/job/136924588396) passed the original failing case; all three matrix lanes passed. Local affected tests and PR CI passed.

A [full nightly rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930544256/job/136927877372) passed the original case and the first four-GPU rollout case, then exposed the same `allreduce:tree` defect inside vLLM's separate inference engine core while profiling a MoE model in `broadcast-32`. That subprocess re-runs vLLM's initializer and fails its own AllGather. Restoring the full lane requires changing the pinned `marin-community/vllm` source setting to include a default algorithm, building a new GPU wheel, and adopting that wheel in Marin. This PR fixes the SkyRL learner side only.

Part of #11955

sourceStates.title: [eval] Send MMLU-Pro's worked examples as conversation turns
sourceStates.body:
MMLU-Pro's few-shot prompt variants now send each worked example as a user turn with its question and an assistant turn with its worked answer, and the question to answer as the last user turn. The instruction stays at the start of the first user turn, and the turn texts concatenate to the one-message prompt that `mmlu_prompt` built, so context fitting keeps the same number of examples. The zero-shot variant is unchanged, and the task's conversation is still the five-shot variant. MMLU-Pro's recipe version gains a `2-` prefix, as `CODE_REVISION` has, so the changed corpus gets a new identity: `curate` identifies the converter by module and name only, and the old version hashed only the scorer files.

With the five examples in one user message, the two Grug checkpoints below answer the worked examples too, and `extract_mmlu_answer` reads the first `answer is (X)`: the first worked example's answer in 8,773 of step 14's 12,032 replies and 6,886 of Campaign2's. Context fitting gives every question five examples when a run's `max_tokens` leaves room for them, as 32,768 does in the protocol's 65,536-token window.

Accuracy on all 12,032 questions, served by vLLM with `skip_special_tokens: false` (as the campaign's configs for both checkpoints set), greedy, `max_tokens` 32,768 and a 73,728-token context. Step 14 is `open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` and Campaign2 is `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10`.

| Run | Step 14 | Campaign2 |
|---|---|---|
| Five examples in one message (main) | 28.8% | 41.3% |
| Row 1's replies, graded on the last `answer is (X)` | 59.7% | 59.6% |
| Five examples as turns | 75.5% | 74.5% |
| Zero-shot | 77.0% | 75.6% |

The runs used #10757's code at 0b2f08b39. Main builds the same one-message prompts: the new test checks that the turns of every variant concatenate to that prompt. Built with this change, the five-shot conversations of all 12,032 questions equal the messages of the turns run, and the zero-shot prompts equal those of the zero-shot run. Evalchemy and TIGER-Lab's API evaluation send the examples in one user message. We have not run the turns on any other model.

The curated `mmlu-pro` evaluation sets no shot count. [`prompt_variant`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb991a5a5c8af4d670d56757eeae3e59edd4a778/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/selection.py#L77-L91) takes the variant with the most examples whose text fits in the 65,536-token window after the run's `max_tokens`, so a run whose `max_tokens` leaves room gets five examples in one message. EvalLite takes the zero-shot variant ([`selection.py` L403-L407](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb991a5a5c8af4d670d56757eeae3e59edd4a778/experiments/post_training/task_curation/selection.py#L403-L407)), which this change leaves as it is. `test_selection.py` read the question from the first message of the five-shot conversation and now reads it from the last.

Part of #10828.

sourceStates.title: [rl-data] Grade nemotron_if with verifyit's IFEval checks
sourceStates.body:
Grade `MarinSkyRL:nemotron_if` with verifyit's IFEval checks instead of the open-instruct checkers in `skyrl/scorers/ifeval_utils.py`. Each Nemotron row becomes a list of verifyit constraints, one per IFEval instruction with the row's non-null arguments, and the grade script still rewards the fraction of constraints passed. RLVR-IFeval keeps its conversion, scorer and rubric.

The open-instruct checkers follow RLVR-IFeval's wording, and three of them fail replies that do what a Nemotron prompt asks: paragraphs divided by `***`, a `***` divider in a reply with an exact bullet count, and a `<<title>>` line above `SECTION 1`. verifyit's checks follow the IFEval wording that these prompts use, and `nemotron_ultra/graders.py` already grades the Nemotron Ultra instruction rows with them.

On the pinned file (`ab2a40d2`, 56,339 rows), conversion keeps 56,083 rows instead of 54,954. `keywords:letter_frequency`, which had no mapping, now converts, and 256 rows are rejected because a required argument is missing or empty. Replies built from each kept row's arguments and the prompt's wording pass 109,315 of 109,316 single-instruction checks; the exception asks for exactly 0 bullets, so its literal reply is blank. Replies that combine `***` paragraphs with bullets pass on all 1,247 rows that ask for both, and a `<<title>>` above the sections passes on all 582. Over the 54,951 rows both versions keep, replies that ignore the prompt earn within 0.0001 of their old mean reward (0.0817 for `yes`, 0.2047 for three unrelated paragraphs). A blank reply earned 0.0822 from constraints such as "no commas" and now scores 0.

`language:response_language` stays unsupported: no row uses it, and verifyit's check passes on a single hint word. The recipe version goes to 2, so pools built before this change keep the old grading until they are rebuilt.

Fixes #11978

sourceStates.title: [rl-data] Align IFEval format checks with Nemotron prompts
sourceStates.body:
The shared SkyRL IFEval format checks now accept `***` and `* * *` as standalone paragraph dividers, exclude those dividers and bold headings from exact bullet counts, count numbered section markers after a title, and count each `**bold**` span once. Replies that omit a required divider, bullet, section marker, or highlight still fail.

The previous checks rejected replies that followed the Nemotron prompts. On the issue's repro inputs, the paragraph, bullet, and section checks returned false, while one bold span passed a request for two highlights; all four results reverse with this change. The shared checker also scores RLVR-IFeval rows, so its format semantics change there too.

[#11979](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11979) separately switches Nemotron grading to verifyit and overlaps with this fix. The two approaches need coordination before either merges.

The affected-test runner reached its 600-second limit after 1,346 passes and 5 skips, with no reported failures. Direct scorer and SkyRL tests passed (15 and 61 cases).

sourceStates.title: [post-training] Consolidate Snowball and Mochi long-loop RL
sourceStates.body:
Keep Snowball and Mochi on one artifact-defined long loop. Consolidate the fifth-round runtime from `benfeuer/exp5-long-loop` at `168cef5e80` and adopted Mochi rounds into the existing SFT, RL, evaluation, publication and archive graph. Round YAMLs pin inputs and topology, render one canonical SkyRL launch document, and retain native best and final checkpoints under permanent storage.

Exp3 now uses the first-fit buffer packer merged in #11379 through `pack_lookahead_window: 128`, retaining the 256-document cap and prediction weights in packed prebuilt caches. This replaces its branch-only policy of selecting the largest fitting document and changes the recipe for future SFT artifact versions. At context 262144/cap 256/window 128, lengths `[160000, 80000, 100000, 180000]` change packs from `[[0,2],[1,3]]` to `[[0,1],[2],[3]]`; padding rises from 4288 to 266432 tokens.

On 100000-document prefixes from #11380's pinned Experiment 2 length vectors, sequence counts change from 5125 to 5130 for math-v3 and 14933 to 14958 for C++; identity stays at 391 sequences but changes membership. These compare Exp3 geometry, not its complete final training mixture. Each frozen 64-document Exp3 CPU smoke source produces the same single pack before and after at production context. Packed prebuilt data now retains the first context-length tokens of oversized singleton documents and discards the remainder; the former packer rejected them. The shared generic packer accepts zero lengths and constrains each cache field independently; the removed wrapper required positive, aligned token and weight lengths. Recompute native sample-origin, truncation and padding accounting under new SFT artifact versions. Existing runs retain their pinned source and recipe.

The Mochi one-rack and three-rack rounds adopt the profile geometry and engine settings from #11321 at `75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9` and #11353 at `e159b10642d1924c400a31bf8160e03ad303f68a`, integrated in `d31b241b65`. Native RL continuation prefers the output version's own latest checkpoint, uses absolute max steps, preserves selection history and resets the elapsed-time training budget in a recovered process, starting its clock after that process completes its first optimizer update. The selected policy requires verifier scores for at least 108 of 120 held-out task attempts. Evaluations run every two updates; each eligible evaluation contributes to an adjusted EMA over up to five observations during warmup, normalized by the available weights. Each improved best is saved immediately. The alternative complete-window policy requires all 120 scores and five consecutive scheduled evaluations.

The bounded acceptance evidence is:

- Snowball 305: 40 GB200s, SFT-to-RL handoff, two committed optimizer updates, evaluation at both updates, protected best at step 1 and final at step 2, with post-archive native retention assertions passing. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-long-loop/long-loop/anchor-snowball-acceptance/archive/2026.11.20.305/ACCEPTED.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop%2Flong-loop%2Fanchor-snowball-acceptance%2Farchive%2F2026.11.20.305%2FACCEPTED.json)).
- Mochi 403: 60 GB200s, the same two-update handoff, eval, native selection and post-archive retention checks. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-long-loop/long-loop/anchor-mochi-acceptance/archive/2026.11.20.403/ACCEPTED.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop%2Flong-loop%2Fanchor-mochi-acceptance%2Farchive%2F2026.11.20.403%2FACCEPTED.json)).
- Serving 502: Mochi SFT step 400407, one 16-GB200 BF16 DP16/EP16 group with FlashInfer and PIECEWISE, 16/16 engines ready in 624.41 seconds, and a 250,034-token rendered input plus 1,024 output tokens. Sampled peak memory was 168.81–169.49 GiB per GPU out of 185.03 GiB. The request took 90.41 seconds, or 11.33 output tokens/second including prefill. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop-acceptance/2026.11.20.502/serving-receipt.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop-acceptance%2F2026.11.20.502%2Fserving-receipt.json)).
- Gate 1 at `e56a0e5840cc463e82375ff61c3f1e0b1deb78e6`: canonical YAML matches the Exp4 recovery launch `2026.11.19.82` (receipt SHA-256 `3cf5793a3de2bda148308500d55f05b1def94d69474e5d322d6741541be67f82`) and the one-rack/three-rack profiles pinned above after 2, 11 and 10 enumerated intended changes, respectively, with no unexplained differences. All five CPU CLI preflights passed. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop-acceptance/gate1-e56a0e58-2026.11.20/result.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop-acceptance%2Fgate1-e56a0e58-2026.11.20%2Fresult.json)).

Both RL runs scored 0.0 on four held-out tasks at each update. They establish pipeline execution and checkpoint selection, with step 1 winning the tie; they provide no evidence of quality improvement. The smokes adopted SFT exports and used bounded rollout budgets. GPU native RL restart, a three-rack RL update, production-sized evaluation cohorts, and sustained serving load remain unverified. Configuration parity uses the anchor compiler and does not establish historical runtime binary equivalence.

General fixes are published independently in #11799–#11809: CP attention validation, registered serving names, startup stack evidence, inference deadlines, export sidecar filtering, initial-model binding, TTL path idempotency, CPU admission, physical GPU placement, redacted command evidence and cancellation notes. The serving probe and startup stack capture are removed from this branch. #11800 carries registered-model identity through the shared inference client, and #11801 carries startup stack capture; the qualified serving harness remains in its sealed experiment evidence. The remaining overlapping implementations stay here until their dependencies land, so the loop remains functional; a later main merge must reconcile their review follow-ups. #11798, the optional permanent-native extension, is withdrawn under the TTL/HF retention decision; this branch keeps its qualified permanent paths as a loop-specific choice. Other general work is already tracked in #11684 (shutdown), #11622 (Pi idle deadlines), #11711 (batch/turn runtime), #11787 (eval provisioning and judge relay), #11659 (curricula), #11379 (packing), #11717/#11751 (FP32 SFT), #11755 (zero-rate parameter drift) and #11750 (restore-gate validation). Those PRs remain in place instead of being duplicated. The retired installed-agent judge argument is already fixed on main by #11704. No duplicate PR was opened for these changes, and #11777 (cache import isolation) is unchanged and excluded from the qualified serving path.

The head preserves anchor history and merges main at `f6484db03743e3a97db162af5ec71844a1edbb47`. Main has since added the RL records and named-evaluation protocol in #10737; that later protocol is not integrated and currently causes merge conflicts. The final head passes CPU construction and parity checks; the GPU receipts above belong to their earlier pinned sources. [The README](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dcfbe879635edcb38d88541bf17e8ea3c60a2583/experiments/post_training/long_loop/README.md) documents round construction, checkpoint and archive contracts, and the CPU preflight interface.

diagnostics.title: [rl] Track the Mochi decode-throughput sprint and pick the RL training config
diagnostics.body:
## TL;DR

A 6-hour optimization sprint (started 2026-11-21 ~13:45 UTC / 8:45 AM EST) measured Mochi (535B-A23B) decode and rollout throughput on GB200s and **selected the training geometry: EP16/DP16/TP1, seq64, HBM 0.85, batch 8192 (A10, 48 trainer + 16 rollout = 64 GB200)** — 2.169x the `.103` control's per-GPU rollout rate. Best pure-decode serving result: EP16/seqs64/HBM90 at 831.73 tok/s/GPU (a fixed-prompt-pool upper bound, not a training gain). The real Mochi RL training launch is planned for 2026-11-21 ~19:45 UTC (14:45 EST) on cw-us-east-08a. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded below with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: the long-loop plan needs ~50B SFT tokens in a 20 h stage plus RL rounds on Mochi. Today Mochi decodes ~10 tok/s per request and ~25 tok/s per GB200 at eval concurrency, and Mochi SFT trains ~143–177k tok/s per rack (#8089: 29.3 s/step on 11 racks). The sprint replaces back-of-envelope ceilings (decode ~2–4k tok/s/GPU BF16 at large batch; training ~2–3x the current rate) with measurements.

Two lanes:

- **A — real-RL rollout arms**: full round-runner RL jobs (48 trainer + 12 rollout GB200, two optimizer updates), measuring rollout throughput under admission knobs; each arm is cancelled after its measured 25-min window.
- **B — pure-decode capacity arms**: no trainer; the checked-in long-loop throughput worker serves a 6.4k-prompt / 1k-output synthetic workload (plus replay variants) and measures sustained decode; arms run to a valid counter window then are cancelled.

Fixed infrastructure for all arms: cluster `cw-us-east-08a`, PRODUCTION priority, GB200 GPUs, rack r136 hard-excluded, one-NVLink-gang placement, BF16, FLASH_ATTN + triton MoE, prefix caching, compilation + PIECEWISE CUDA graphs on.

Workload-shape caveat for the B serving lane: the fixed-pool shared8 arms use 32 prompt bodies / 256 request identities at 6,439 input / 1,024 output tokens (long) or 139 input (short); repeated cycles can overstate fresh-RL prefix reuse. Pure serving runs use 12 GPUs unless the arm name says EP16 (then 16). All B arms use 0 Daytona vCPU.

### Reproduction

- Repo: `marin-community/marin`, branch `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` and sprint branch `benfeuer/mochi-throughput`.
- Round configs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-*.yaml` (default-2update, inflight128, staleness11, engine32-kv85, harbor1024, harbor384, ep16-seqs64, ep16-seqs64-kv90, ep16-httpid-control, noquotas, kv-fp8, **ep16-demand512** `.118`, **train** `.115`; the retired workers128 config was deleted unlaunched).
- Decode specs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/mochi-decode-*.json` (seqs16 control through the ep16 variants).
- Launch commands:
  - Real-RL arm: `uv run --no-sync python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop.round_runner --round experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/<arm>.yaml --source-revision <git-sha> --validation-output <path> --through rl --run`
  - Pure-decode arm: `uv run --no-sync python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop.throughput` with the pinned spec JSON, submitted via the standard Iris CLI (source-pinned launch specs under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-throughput/launches/<sha>/`).
- Source revisions: v103 `b0a9727622d54a75101c455f3e304d6ae3003565`; seqs32 `.104` `46063946b49d9d677f5aa0c94a26f27715550764`; A1 `.105` `476a95362f35014e5d092ebd79adfcd542cb5105`; A2 `.106` `3bc5ae3fda43203232aa2c2dc019e8abeea5a69d`; A3 `.107` and first EP16 pair `3a859712f51d3ddff46748e850208e8315dc53da`; harbor1024 `.108` config-landed `e0bf304558d4fdbf3b41a9b68285918eb19ca1ca` (actually submitted at `3f4a4c68ce…`); harbor384 `.109` `c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d`; workers128 `.110` `7f245b01735ced953e3ce490db8bca9159bc0d1f`; `.110`-default3 re-land `8aee017ea5cfcd9748c372fc8555be2c8483f757`; B kv90 landing `530ab73b76a28a3e15a741d8f946a0dfaeea8818`; `.111` real EP16 arm `058da8dcc2332525d6245ba8f7bae6ea18308b4c`; `.112` quota-free `aab5e5f57bfa1ef5a6cb3c599ba40302a8e92247`; `.113` A9 kv90 real with header fix `858ab5d15bf3118ae0358ff79569ec6b33320a68`; `.113`-recipe landing `f26fc27bcd86dac16bcf867435f72ef9166cf463`; final-gates landing `cf7e04df26c99f74e52d5c39e3cb7b6e593ea8e1`; **selected-training landing `5957d8bbcf0cd945243cdd544eb4433f7e36ac88`**; A11 FP8-KV `ce13e39e8435a9149a1268d6b25db54c32f75411`; A13 demand-512 `dd0250dc1a65a3e04c2f6b0d2f79ea55511a506f`; **relaunch `.119` `ccf0bdc3561be7b3a6d407b3c95af03fbf37f2c4`**; **correction `.120` `6a118946e605a3eba586b0d256139a6690a859cc`**; quota-free fix `30d6357c550d35617b49e9f0c630c3754d7c87f2`; observation fix `3226044a8fcf1dacad4b022074f94784493f83b7`; Daytona ownership metric `8b1e1686a985691f9454ed2c01c757c79f3ec736`; context-gap fix `119ea9984b7e400e926ced96bc8a4a3f8df0a11b`; latest B pair `3f4a4c68ce4fad43d1a639d1d390d1ae3e3649b1`; pure-decode implementation landing `e9a16e37ce65754192208551df44e972e8c9de7b`. Per-arm B serving sources differ (KV85 `f91a4966b6…`, batch16384 `476a95362f…`, shared8 pair `d08bf17b3a…`, seqs64 pair `3bc5ae3fda…`) — the machine-readable index is `secretary-arm-provenance-20261121.json` in the evidence folder.
- Counters: the engine-side Finelog sink registered by SkyRL's `inference_stats` callback (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/callbacks/builtin.py:1253` and `:1108`; `inference_observability.py:130`), read as reset-safe cumulative deltas over fixed windows. A1–A3 lack native `generation_tokens_total` because the recipes' explicit callback list makes `create_default_callbacks` return early, so their rates are console-sample estimates (marked * in the table). The callback is added from A4 and the training config onward. Example queries: `decode-control-live-samples-1308.jsonl` + `analyze_decode_live.py` (control window 12:58:49–13:07:52 UTC: 1,341,242 generated-token increments over 542.47 s = 2,472.48 tok/s aggregate), `a3-first25-analysis.json`.
- Receipts: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-throughput/...` (Filer links below) and local evidence folder `/Users/benfeuer/Documents/experiments/active/mochi-throughput/`.

### Rollout concurrency (code trace)

- `TaskRolloutWorker` holds `task_slots` and `harbor_task_slots` semaphores (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py:390-391`), acquired per task (`:548-552`); the Harbor semaphore wraps the entire `engine.run_task`.
- Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` is consumed at `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inline_harbor_client.py:119`.
- Documented rule: slots = Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` (16 when unset) // num workers (`lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:458`); config key `terminal_bench.harbor.n_concurrent_trials` (`experiments/post_training/long_loop/stage_config.py:38`). For the 256-slot config that is 8/worker; Harbor384 gives 12/worker.
- Precision: the 8-slot semaphore is one group's worth, not an atomic group lock — partial groups can interleave; dispatch `min(_pending)` has no Harbor-slot awareness, and the generic 1024/worker task slots are unbinding.
- Measurement limit: no explicit Harbor-semaphore wait logs are emitted, and A5's bounded logs contain 0 direct slot-wait records, so actual Harbor occupancy is NOT measured; A3's 128 group calls / 430 pending model requests do not count Harbor occupancy.
- Staleness admission: `FullBatch.lease_batch` uses `range(step, step + staleness + 1)`, so staleness can change admission during step 1 even without a policy update (this corrects an earlier blanket "never binds" statement; the A2 causal-gain claim remains withdrawn and default staleness 3 is kept per direction).
- Consumed route quotas require `batch_policy: full_batch` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/buffer.py:49,72`; `lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:440,444`).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Pick the real Mochi RL training config from measurements: rollout throughput as a function of admission knobs (inflight workers, max_staleness_steps, Harbor slots) and decode throughput as a function of engine knobs (max_num_seqs, HBM/KV utilization, expert parallelism, shared-prefix layout, batched tokens). Decision rule (user ruling): config changes only — no engine code changes.

## Status

- Sprint clock: started ~13:45 UTC 2026-11-21; training selection 19:30 UTC (14:30 EST); real RL launch 19:45 UTC (14:45 EST).
- Current **provisional training candidate** (worker statement, 13:43 EST / 18:45 UTC): **EP12, seq32, HBM 0.85, batch 8192, Harbor 256, workers 32, inflight128, staleness 3, graphs/prefix caching ON** — the quota on/off choice pends the 19:30 evidence (A9/A10 finals). Framing: A3's engine first-25min estimate (127.22/GPU vs the `.103` control's 55.90) is a 2.28x OBSERVED short-window/proxy (staleness 11 in A3 is not retained for training); A8's quota-off 208.63/GPU is a 3.73x OBSERVED raw rate but with 0 consumed batches / 90 nonagentic completions, so it is NOT a training gain. Earlier "current training candidate" notes are superseded by this reconciled statement.
- Two follow-up decode arms in flight at source `3f4a4c68ce`: EP16/seqs128/shared8 (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs128-shared8-20261121a`) and EP16/seqs64/batch4096/shared8 (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs64-batch4096-shared8-20261121a`).
- In flight at ~17:10 UTC: A5/Harbor384 engine init completed 17:09 UTC (no generation counter window yet; startup receipts `sprint-current-startup-1709.jsonl`, `sprint-a5-live-1709.jsonl`); both B EP16 arms loaded weights 17:07–17:09 UTC (`sprint-b-live-1709.jsonl`). A B HBM 0.90 arm was then submitted in parallel (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs64-kv90-shared8-20261121a`, 16 GB200, source `530ab73b76a28a3e15a741d8f946a0dfaeea8818`, spec `mochi-decode-ep16-seqs64-kv90-shared8.json` — only change HBM 0.85→0.90 versus the completed EP16/seqs64 552.15 tok/s/GPU baseline), since A60 + B16×3 = 108 ≤ the 128-GPU cap.
- **B batch4096 FINAL** (valid 1500.818 s window, zero failed requests; 18,553 overlapping requests valid; drain 123.564 s): 12,016.76 aggregate / **751.05 tok/s/GPU**, request arithmetic mean 12.21 tok/s, 61.59/64 running, KV 52.41% mean / 65.58% max, TTFT 3.20 s, prefix hit 99.76% — **+36.02%** over the EP16/seqs64 batch8192 baseline (552.15/GPU; request 9.27→12.21, KV 85.43→52.41, prefix 48.86→99.76). This fixed-32-shared-prompt-pool cache-fit gain is NOT yet a real-RL gain (receipt `pure-ep16-batch4096-result.json`; final artifact `decode/ep16-seqs64-kv85-batch4096-shared8-20261121a/synthetic-context64-output1024-shared8-seed17-c1024.json`). **Correction (~20:15 UTC): kv90's final 831.73/GPU is the best valid long-B** — batch4096's 751.05 is second; the early kv90 provisional (844.22) had overstated its final. Sequencing: A7 runs its specified batch 8192 first; the best one-knob B candidate follows in real rollouts.
- **A5/Harbor384 FINAL 25-min** (17:19:36–17:44:36 UTC, all 12 ranks, 0 resets): 1499.61 aggregate / **124.97 tok/s/GPU** native, 30.84/32 running + 11.26 waiting, KV 67.26%, request 4.04, TTFT 53.04 s; last 10 min 105.61/GPU (29.94/32 running, KV 85.30%). Matched-method comparison: A5 raw console first-20 ~133.01/GPU vs A3 raw 134.876 (−1.4%, no gain); A5 raw first-25 127.35 vs A3 console 127.22 (~flat, baseline driver-dedup). More Harbor capacity (256→384) did not improve early-window throughput — engines were already full/queued (receipts `a5-final25-analysis.json`, `a5-all-engine-raw-stats-1744.json`, `a5-native-final25-1744.jsonl`).
- Still provisional: none — all three B EP16 finals are in (seq128 443.95/GPU; batch4096 751.05/GPU; kv90 831.73/GPU, all zero errors; both seq128/kv90 cancelled-own 17:54:58–59 UTC). **B is paused; A7 is running; quota-free A8 is validating/submitting now on the new source — parallel A7+A8 = 124 GPU.** No Harbor-1024 or workers128 launch; the 12:13 Harbor384 direction stands.
- **Engine-side context split** (prompt vs decode, same engine): A5/Harbor384 native 25-min — **1,663.40 prompt tok/s/GPU vs 124.97 decode**, 66 KV preemptions, token-weighted prefix hit 19.575% (not the console 33% rank mean), completed-request prefill mean 1.727 s vs decode 86.739 s (n=3551). 93.0% of tokens are prompt — but that is NOT 93% of GPU time. A3 raw first-20 (all 12 engines): estimated 1,218.73 prompt vs 134.88 decode tok/s/GPU; 8 retained driver request-rate samples median 3.40 / mean 3.54 tok/s (dedup-biased, not population). A3's running-context distribution and exact preemptions were not retained (timing-slack prompt length, callback off). Context gap fixed for the next arm: `119ea9984b7e400e926ced96bc8a4a3f8df0a11b` via loop-push — existing timing events get numeric prompt/context tokens from pinned vLLM `state.prompt_len` (not prompt text); public-evidence unit test/lint pass.
- A4 (Harbor 1024) was submitted and immediately cancelled under a new shared-quota rule (budget: 6000 vCPU, 30 sandbox creates/s, 4 CPU per sandbox). Its replacement A4/Harbor384 (`.109`) is submitted: `/benfeuer/long-loop-mochi-throughput-harbor384-2026.11.21.109-coordinator-16513921` (60 GB200), source `c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d`, config `rounds/mochi-throughput-harbor384.yaml` (Harbor 256→384 only, 32 workers; ≤1536 vCPU worst case), native `inference_stats` counters on; A3 was cancelled once measured.
- The 128-worker client arm (`.110`) was landed and validated but **retired unlaunched** per the user's 12:13 EST direction: A3 already queued model demand and showed a non-GIL CPU profile, so the client-cap question is answered without it; no job was submitted (final recipe source `8aee017ea5cfcd9748c372fc8555be2c8483f757`, compiled staleness 3 confirmed) and the recipe was subsequently deleted.
- The `.111` real EP16 arm is landed and validated, and is now **submitted as A7**: `rounds/mochi-throughput-ep16-seqs64.yaml` at source `058da8dcc2332525d6245ba8f7bae6ea18308b4c` (later refreshed preflights passed on `3226044a8f…` and `8b1e1686a9…`) — seq64/EP16/DP16/TP1, HBM 0.85, batch 8192, Harbor384, staleness 3, workers 32, inflight128, native `inference_stats`. Job: `/benfeuer/long-loop-mochi-throughput-ep16-seqs64-2026.11.21.111-coordinator-22f1e6e8` (48 trainer + 16 rollout = 64 GB200, PRODUCTION 08a, r136 excluded, graphs on). The measured A5/Harbor384 was cancelled at 17:45:29 UTC; its final receipt is pending. Quota-free A8 (`.112`) launches next as remaining B measurement/drain releases capacity (parallel A7+A8 = 124 GPU).
- Per the user's 12:18 EST direction, a **quota-off** arm (`.112`) is landed: `rounds/mochi-throughput-noquotas.yaml` at source `aab5e5f57bfa1ef5a6cb3c599ba40302a8e92247` with `consumed_route_quotas{}` (empty — quotas off) while keeping `batch_policy: full_batch`, seq32/HBM 0.85, Harbor 256, workers 32, inflight128, staleness 3, native `inference_stats`. diagnostics.body:
## TL;DR

A ~12-hour PRODUCTION-priority sprint (opened 2026-11-21 ~23:00 EST per the user request) to (1) maximize Snowball decode throughput at the 65,536-token request window and (2) size the Snowball RL job as small as possible while keeping training saturated (rollout wait near zero, no time-per-update regression vs the current baseline). Deliverable: a right-sized Snowball RL layout (GPU counts, engine config, all gates) with its measured time per update vs the current allocation and the GPU-hours cost per update. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded as it lands with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: Snowball RL runs on the Exp4/Exp5 long-loop pools (H100 on cw-rno2a; Snowball also ran on cw-us-east-08a GB200 for the Nov 20 acceptance, job `.305`, 40 GB200). The playbook and lessons come from the Mochi sprint (#11954, closed) and its concurrency-gate table (#11957).

Two phases:
- **Phase 1 — decode throughput at 65k context**: pure serving-benchmark arms with the exact Snowball RL rollout engine config, measured with native vLLM counters (aggregate and per-GPU generated tok/s, per-request tok/s, running/waiting per engine, KV use, prefix-hit rate, preemptions, TTFT) on a long-prompt 65,536-token workload with group-shared prompts as in RL.
- **Phase 2 — right-size the RL job**: shrink rollout GPUs and trainer GPUs step by step on real rollouts with the current Snowball curriculum (Exp4/Exp5 pools); report time per update, rollout wait, engine occupancy, and the per-step split (rollout wait / optimizer / checkpoint / eval). Saturated = trainer rollout wait per step near zero and time per update not regressing vs baseline.

Fixed infrastructure/rules for all arms: PRODUCTION priority; GPU budget ≤ ~2 racks / 128 GPUs in flight without coordinator approval; do not disturb Exp5 SFT (256 H100 on cw-rno2a); one knob per arm, config over code; each arm cancelled with `iris-cancel-own` once measured (25-min windows); Harbor ≤ 512 (Daytona RL org shared, one job ~1/4–1/3 of its 6,000 vCPU); long jobs' IDs go to the coordinator watchdog, no polling loops.

diagnostics.title: [skyrl] Unify the rollout concurrency limits into one explicit budget
diagnostics.body:
SkyRL RL rollouts have about a dozen independent limits on how much work generates at once. Several have coupled defaults, so changing one knob silently moves another, and the engine throughput of a run depends on whichever one binds first. In the Mochi throughput sprint (#11954) the binding limit changed three times as we raised knobs one at a time, and each change needed a code read to explain.

Limits on the rollout path (paths relative to `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/`, read at `3a859712f5` on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype`; the same code is on `main`):

| Layer | Knob | What it caps |
|---|---|---|
| Buffer (`rollouts/buffer.py`) | `trainer.rollout_buffer.max_in_flight` | Prompt groups generating at once, across all routes. When null, an Iris launch derives it as 1.5 batches, capped at Harbor `n_concurrent_trials / n_samples_per_prompt` (`config/ppo_base_config.yaml:248-251`), so 256 / 8 = 32. |
| Buffer | `max_staleness_steps` with `batch_policy: full_batch` | How many batches generation may lease ahead of training (`FullBatchRolloutPolicy.lease_batch`). This binds during step 1, because the step waits for its slowest group. |
| Buffer | `consumed_route_quotas` | Agentic and nonagentic groups per batch. `experiments/post_training/long_loop/nvl72.py` overwrote an explicit `{}` with `batch_size // 2` each until `30d6357c55`. |
| Worker pool (`rollouts/workers.py`) | `trajectory_runner.rollout_workers.num_workers`, `cpus_per_worker` | Not a cap by itself, because workers are async actors. It divides the Harbor cap into per-worker shares, and `num_workers * cpus_per_worker` must fit the driver node's CPUs. |
| Task worker (`rollouts/task_worker.py:390-395, 763`) | `trajectory_runner.max_concurrent_tasks` | Trajectories per worker (1,024 by default). |
| Task worker | `terminal_bench.harbor.n_concurrent_trials // num_workers` | Harbor-routed trajectories per worker, held for the whole trial. The pool dispatches groups to the least-loaded worker with no regard to free Harbor slots (`workers.py:271-275`). |
| Task worker | `rollout_workers.executor_threads`, `task_sessions.max_verifier_workers` | Blocking-operation and verifier threads per worker (256 and 32 by default). |
| Graders | `_SYMBOLIC_SLOTS = BoundedSemaphore(8)` (`skyrl-gym/.../math_with_judge.py:62`), GenRM `max_concurrent_comparisons`, teacher-oracle capacity | Grading throughput for specific sources. |
| External | Daytona org quota and create rate, remote judge rate limits, vLLM `max_num_seqs` / `gpu_memory_utilization` / `max_num_batched_tokens` | Sandboxes, judge calls, and engine slots. |

Observed effect, all on Mochi on cw-us-east-08a with 12 rollout GB200 GPUs:
- The baseline (`max_in_flight` 32, the derived default) ran at about 56 generated tok/s per GPU.
- Raising `max_in_flight` to 128 doubled that for about 25 minutes, then it fell to 34 tok/s per GPU when the staleness lookahead ran out.
- Raising staleness let the engines fill up (30 of 32 sequences running per engine). At that point vLLM capacity became the limit.

Each of these needed a separate code trace to explain.

Done when: the rollout path has one documented concurrency budget, from which the per-resource limits (Harbor sandboxes, judge calls, verifier threads) are derived or explicitly declared. A run logs, at startup, the effective value of every limit in the table. At runtime, it logs which limit blocked admission.

diagnostics.title: [levanter] Make the forced final checkpoint save crash-safe on temporary and restarted runs
diagnostics.body:
Follow-up to #11534. #11552 fixed the `--permanent` case of the forced final checkpoint save. Two cases still leave the step that discovery selects unloadable if the process dies while `manifest.json` is open:

- **Default mode:** the last save was temporary and `temporary_base_path` is unset.
- **Restart:** a completed run is restarted. A new `Checkpointer` starts with `_last_save_step = 0`, so the forced hooks in `train()` rewrite the step they just loaded, whether that step was saved as permanent or temporary.

In both cases `step-N/manifest.json` is truncated, and loading fails with `ValidationError: ... Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value`.

We tested the fix proposed in #11534 (items 1 and 3 from the issue body) on `main` at `cb991a5`, CPU only, local file system. Both items are needed. Item 1 alone fixes every crash point we tested. Item 3 alone fails the restart cases, because it relies on in-memory `_last_save_*` state that a new `Checkpointer` does not have. Item 3 also removes the whole re-save in the default mode, which closes the untested window where the array data is re-written.

Does the step selected by discovery load after the kill?

| Mode | `main` | Item 1 only | Item 3 only | Items 1 + 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (last save temporary, `temporary_base_path` unset) | fail | pass | pass (no re-save) | pass (no re-save) |
| `--permanent` | pass (#11552) | pass | pass | pass |
| `--restart` (last step temporary) | fail | pass | fail | pass |
| `--restart --permanent` | fail; no loadable checkpoint remains | pass | fail | pass |

`uv run --package marin-levanter --group test pytest tests -k checkpoint -x -q` (from `lib/levanter`): 115 passed with both items applied.

## Required changes

1. **Write `manifest.json` atomically on local paths** in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint_manifest.py` `write_manifest`. Do this through `rigging.filesystem.atomic.atomic_rename`, as `_save_metadata` does for `metadata.json`. Remote paths (GCS/S3) keep the plain write: object stores publish an object only when its write completes, and `atomic_rename` on S3 would be a copy plus delete, which protected prefixes deny.
2. **Promote a forced save instead of re-saving** in `Checkpointer.on_step` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py`). This applies when `force` is set, `step` equals `_last_save_step`, and `temporary_base_path` is None:
   - wait for the pending save;
   - rewrite only `metadata.json` with `is_temporary=False` through `_save_metadata(..., extra_metadata=self.metadata)`;
   - on process 0, drop that path from `_temporary_checkpoints` and prune with keep=0;
   - set `_last_save_permanent = True`, and return.

   When `temporary_base_path` is set, keep today's behavior: a fresh `base_path/step-N` write never touches a committed directory.
3. **Initialize `_last_save_step` to `None`**, not `0`. Without this, change 2 makes a forced step-0 save on a new `Checkpointer` look "already saved", and `step-0/` is never written. That breaks `test_train_lm_initialize_model_from_checkpoint`.

Keep the diff limited to these three changes. The tested diff is +21/−1 across two files:

<details><summary>Tested diff against cb991a5</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py
index 5acffef01f..4db5031864 100644
--- a/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py
+++ b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py
@@ -527,7 +527,7 @@ class Checkpointer:
         self.keep_params = keep_params
         self._dt_now_injection = dt_now_injection or datetime.datetime.now
         self._last_save_time = self._dt_now_injection()
-        self._last_save_step = 0
+        self._last_save_step: int | None = None
         self._last_save_permanent = False
         self.keep_last_temporary_checkpoints = keep_last_temporary_checkpoints
         self.debug = debug or CheckpointDebugConfig()
@@ -619,6 +619,17 @@ class Checkpointer:
             # The final hook must still surface a failed pending save before later hooks run.
             self._manager.wait_until_finished()
             return
+        if force and step == self._last_save_step and self.temporary_base_path is None:
+            # This step's temporary save already committed step-N/ under base_path. Promote it to permanent
+            # by rewriting only metadata.json instead of re-serializing into the committed directory.
+            self._manager.wait_until_finished()
+            checkpoint_path = os.path.join(self.base_path, f"step-{step}")
+            _save_metadata(checkpoint_path, step, is_temporary=False, extra_metadata=self.metadata)
+            if jax.process_index() == 0:
+                self._temporary_checkpoints = [r for r in self._temporary_checkpoints if r.path != checkpoint_path]
+                self._prune_temporary_checkpoints(0)
+            self._last_save_permanent = True
+            return
 
         my_should_save = force or requested_retention is not None
         my_save_permanent_ckpt = force or requested_retention == CheckpointRetention.PERMANENT
diff --git a/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint_manifest.py b/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint_manifest.py
```

## Reproduction harness

This is a variant of the #11534 script. It kills the process when the forced save opens, for writing, any file in `step-N/` whose name starts with `manifest.json`, so the `atomic_rename` temporary file `manifest.json.tmp.<hex>` counts too. The issue's original script only matches `manifest.json` exactly, so it can no longer fire once the write goes through a temporary file. `--restart` saves cleanly in run 1, then makes the forced save from a fresh `Checkpointer` in run 2, as a restarted completed run does. `--crash-on=metadata.json` tests the metadata window.

<details><summary>resave_harness.py</summary>

```python
"""Variant of the #11534 script.

  python resave_harness.py [--permanent] [--restart] [--crash-on=manifest.json]

Kills the process when the forced re-save opens, for writing, any file in step-N/ whose basename starts
with the --crash-on prefix (so the atomic_rename temporary file manifest.json.tmp.<hex> also counts).
--restart: run 1 saves steps 1..N and exits cleanly; run 2 builds a fresh Checkpointer (as a restarted
completed run does) and makes the forced save; run 3 discovers and loads.
"""
import builtins
import datetime
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import jax.numpy as jnp
from levanter.checkpoint import Checkpointer, CheckpointInterval, latest_checkpoint_path, load_checkpoint

STATE = {"model": jnp.arange(4.0)}
LAST = 2 if "--permanent" in sys.argv else 3
RESTART = "--restart" in sys.argv
PREFIX = next((a.split("=", 1)[1] for a in sys.argv if a.startswith("--crash-on=")), "manifest.json")


def checkpointer(base):
    return Checkpointer(base, save_interval=datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1),
                        step_policies=[CheckpointInterval(every=2)])


def install_crash():
    real_open = builtins.open
    target_dir = f"step-{LAST}"

    def crashing_open(file, mode="r", *args, **kwargs):
        f = real_open(file, mode, *args, **kwargs)
        p = str(file)
        if ("w" in mode or "a" in mode) and os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(p)) == target_dir \
                and os.path.basename(p).startswith(PREFIX):
            print(f"killing at open of {os.path.basename(p)}", flush=True)
            os._exit(137)
        return f

    builtins.open = crashing_open


def save_steps(ckpt):
    for step in range(1, LAST + 1):
        time.sleep(0.01)
        ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=step)
        ckpt.wait_until_finished()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["save"]:
        save_steps(checkpointer(sys.argv[2]))
        sys.exit(0)
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["crash"]:
        ckpt = checkpointer(sys.argv[2])
        if not RESTART:
            save_steps(ckpt)
        install_crash()
        ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=LAST, force=True)
        ckpt.wait_until_finished()
        sys.exit("not killed")

    base = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    extra = sys.argv[1:]
    if RESTART:
        rc0 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, "save", base] + extra).returncode
        print(f"run 1 (clean) exit {rc0}; checkpoints: {sorted(os.listdir(base))}", flush=True)
    rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, "crash", base] + extra).returncode
    print(f"forced-save run exit {rc}; checkpoints: {sorted(os.listdir(base))}; step-{LAST}/: "
          f"{sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(base, f'step-{LAST}')))}", flush=True)
    path = latest_checkpoint_path(base)
    print(f"latest checkpoint: {os.path.basename(path)}", flush=True)
    try:
        load_checkpoint(STATE, path)
        print("loaded")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"load failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}")
```
</details>

Run with `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu uv run --package marin-levanter python resave_harness.py [--permanent] [--restart] [--crash-on=<prefix>]`. With both changes applied, every mode prints `latest checkpoint: step-N` and `loaded`.

## Known limits (not in scope)

- A crash leaves `manifest.json.tmp.<hex>` or `metadata.json.tmp.<hex>` in `step-N/`. Loading ignores it, and only deleting the step removes it. #10969's cleanup removes only `*.__lock` files.
- In the restart case, the array data is still re-written. Only the `manifest.json` window is protected there; a crash while the data is re-written is untested.
- Multi-process runs are untested. Only process 0 writes `manifest.json`. The new branch depends on per-process `_last_save_*` state, which follows the broadcast save decision.

Done when:
- a PR applies the three changes above, with a behavior test for the default and restart cases (a crash during the forced save leaves the selected step loadable);
- `pytest tests -k checkpoint` passes in `lib/levanter`;
- the PR closes this issue and #11534.

diagnostics.title: [rl-data] nemotron_if fails replies that follow its paragraph instruction
diagnostics.body:
`MarinSkyRL:nemotron_if` maps each Nemotron IFEval instruction to an open-instruct checker in `skyrl/scorers/ifeval_utils.py` (`NEMOTRON_CONSTRAINTS` in `skyrl/ifeval.py`). For three instructions the checker's rule differs from the prompt's wording, so a reply that does what the prompt says fails the constraint. The source is 15% of the RL groups in the Exp4 curriculum (#11681), whose pools Exp5 reuses.

| Instruction | Prompt | Checker | Rows that fail |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `length_constraints:number_paragraphs` | "Paragraphs are separated with the markdown divider: ***" | `verify_paragraph_count` splits on `* * *` only, so a reply divided by `***` has one paragraph | 4,515 (every row that asks for 2 or more) |
| the same rows that also ask for an exact `number_bullet_lists` | "exactly N bullet points ... such as: * This is point 1." | `verify_bullet_points` counts every line that starts with `*`, so each `***` divider line is a bullet too | 1,211 of 1,218 lose both constraints |
| `multiple_sections` with `detectable_format:title` | "Mark the beginning of each section with SECTION X" | `validate_sections` counts the text before the first marker as a section, so a `<<title>>` line above `SECTION 1` adds one | 554 |

Two more differences depend on how a reply is formatted. A line that opens with markdown bold, such as `**Key points:**`, counts as a bullet, and 15,316 rows ask for an exact bullet count. `validate_highlighted_sections` counts each `**bold**` span twice, so half the requested highlights pass; 19,355 rows ask for two or more.

The counts are over the pinned file (`nvidia/Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset` at `ab2a40d2`, `RL/instruction_following/instruction_following.jsonl`, 56,339 rows) run through `nemotron_constraint` and `normalize_ground_truth` at `cd0e932c7`, which keep 54,954 rows; the Exp4 pool in `exp4_data.py` records 54,953. For each kept row I built replies from the row's own arguments and the prompt's wording and scored them against the row's constraints. 4,625 of the 4,723 prompts with the paragraph instruction write the divider as `***`, and none writes only `* * *`. verifyit's IFEval checks (`lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py`) pass every one of these replies.

On the 4,515 paragraph rows, a reply that follows the instruction and a reply that ignores it both fail the constraint, so it gives RL no signal toward following it; only a reply that happens to use `* * *` passes.

Reproduce from the repository root with plain `python`:

```python
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers")
import ifeval_utils as checks

reply = "First paragraph.\n\n***\n\nSecond paragraph."
print(checks.verify_paragraph_count(reply, 2))  # False
print(checks.verify_paragraph_count(reply.replace("***", "* * *"), 2))  # True

with_bullets = "First paragraph.\n* One\n* Two\n\n***\n\nSecond paragraph."
print(checks.verify_bullet_points(with_bullets, 2))  # False: the divider line also starts with *

titled = "<<A Title>>\n\nSECTION 1\nBody.\n\nSECTION 2\nBody."
print(checks.validate_sections(titled, 2, "SECTION"))  # False: the title line counts as a section
```

Expected: a reply that follows the prompt's wording passes these constraints.

cc @penfever @chrismc91

Record the active Snowball baseline from the worker's pinned source, resolved round, job ID, trainer and rollout GPU counts, engine TP/DP/EP, memory fraction, sequence and batch limits, and every effective concurrency gate. Measure completed update times, rollout wait, optimizer, checkpoint, and eval time on the current Exp4/Exp5 curriculum; publish the receipt before comparing arms.
2. Run 65,536-token serving arms with group-shared prompts and the baseline engine config through `throughput.py`. Change one of memory fraction, `max_num_seqs`, expert parallelism, or batched tokens per arm; keep 25-minute counter windows and report generated tokens/s per GPU, request rate, running/waiting, KV use, prefix hit, preemptions, and TTFT. Mark incomplete or error-heavy windows inconclusive; check any TP or quantization candidate against BF16 logprobs before using its rate.
3. Carry the best valid serving candidate into real rollouts, then reduce rollout GPUs and trainer GPUs one step at a time while holding curriculum, staleness, route quotas, and checkpoint/eval cadence fixed. Compare complete optimizer updates against the baseline; report rollout wait and the per-step time split, plus GPU-hours/update = total allocated GPUs × seconds/update ÷ 3600.
4. Select the smallest layout whose rollout wait remains near zero and whose update time does not regress within the observed variation. Publish the chosen GPU counts, full engine and gate configuration, source commit, launch commands, Iris IDs, Finelog windows, receipts, baseline comparison, and cost on this issue and the linked logbook.
